{
  "title": "First Open Source Contribution: Start with Documentation",
  "body_markdown": "Hey all! If you're new to open source, it's totally okay to start small. One of the easiest ways to contribute is by updating or adding documentation. It’s helpful, appreciated, and low-risk!\n\nHere’s a practical example:\n\n1. **Find a project**: Look for a project that’s welcoming to newcomers and check if they need documentation updates.\n2. **Read the guidelines**: Many projects have a CONTRIBUTING.md file. Read it to understand how to submit your changes.\n3. **Spot an issue**: Identify a documentation issue, like a typo, missing explanation, or outdated link.\n4. **Make your changes**: Edit the documentation file in your local clone, or open a new issue if the change is too big.\n5. **Submit a pull request**: Once you’re happy with your edits, open a pull request (PR).\n\n**Concrete takeaway**: Even small documentation updates can make a big difference! Here’s how you can format a simple code example in markdown:\n\n```python\n# Example: Printing Hello, World!\nprint('Hello, World!')\n```\n\nRemember, every contribution counts! Celebrate your small wins along the way. Happy coding!
